newsitem.title: UK: Northern Irish bomb warning a hoax.
newsitem.headline: Northern Irish bomb warning a hoax.

text.p: British security forces sealed off an area of Londonderry city in Northern Ireland on Monday after a bomb alert which turned out to be a hoax.

Several houses were evacuated in a street in the Catholic nationalist Bogside area after "a suspicious object" was found taped to railings and a telephone warning was received in the early hours of Monday morning.
But police said later they had been the victims of an "elaborate hoax" and the alert was called off.
The alert came a few hours before the resumption in Belfast of multi-party talks on the future of the British-ruled province.
Worsening guerrilla violence and the prospect of a general election in Britain and Northern Ireland within the next four months have soured hopes of progress at the talks.
The IRA, which draws support from Catholic strongholds, has recently intensified an armed campaign to end British rule, targeting police and soldiers.
Protestant Loyalist extremists, who support British rule, have been blamed by police chiefs for three bomb attacks on Catholics since December.
